answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by making each identity expensive to create: before an agent may transact, it must lock a refundable deposit in a shared vault, bonded to a single verifiable keypair. A cipher-based proof links every action to that bonded key, so one operator running a thousand fake agents must fund a thousand deposits. Misbehavior slashes the bond, while honest agents earn it back over time. Like a sonnet, the rules are strict but simple: the cost scales linearly with the number of identities, so flooding the network stops being profitable.
